stories.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
stories.author: hecmmm

topComments.author: hecmmm
topComments.text: Abstract: We propose a background independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes. Starting from first order gravity, we solve the gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain the reduced phase space at finite GN. We promote its canonical Poisson brackets to commutation relations and use deformations of the reduced action to define an algebra of observables. Equipped with this, we use Gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs to construct a nonperturbative Hilbert space representation, for which this algebra generates a type I factor. By composing amplitudes between states prepared on null cones, we then obtain a Lorentzian path integral in which each sum over intermediate states converges absolutely. As a check, we compute the amplitude for graviton pair creation and annihilation on a null cone nonperturbatively in GN and find a finite closed form expression, even though expanding first in GN yields a logarithmic divergence. We next use diffeomorphism invariance of the path integral to show that a macroscopic causal diamond with a given maximum size has a finite dimensional Hilbert space. From the Lorentzian trace we obtain the Bekenstein Hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces and calculate its logarithmic correction for large Schwarzschild black holes, recovering at one loop the coefficient Sen obtained through Euclidean methods. We end by deriving the semiclassical Einstein equations to one loop as the low energy limit of this theory.

jobs.author: Kiran_MixRank
jobs.title: MixRank (YC S11) | Software Engineers | 100% Remote (Global) | Full-Time MixRank processes petabytes of data every month through web crawling. Hundreds of customers use our data products, including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries such as finance, recruiting, sales, marketing, and security. We’re a fully remote company with a global footprint across 20+ countries. We’re growing, profitable, employee-owned, and have no dependence on outside funding. Applicants from all geographies and backgrounds are welcome. We’re looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job, but something they genuinely love to do. We’re obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team. Our codebase is friendly to new contributors. You’ll have a fully functional development environment within hours through full automation and will be pushing commits on your first day. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in under two minutes.Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you’ll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git. We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We run two datacenters with high-performance servers we’ve built ourselves, capable of handling the volumes of data we process. We’ve implemented our own distributed file system, perform full-scale web crawls, and download and run static analysis on the entire universe of published Android APKs and iOS IPAs.
jobs.text: Unlike a typical startup where you might spend half your time in meetings and the other half fixing Jira tickets, at MixRank you’ll challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that help you grow as an individual. We’re continuously hiring for the positions below; these aren’t singular roles that close once filled. Our philosophy is that the candidate is more important than the position. For each new member of the team, we design a custom role and responsibilities around their interests. Other companies may create a long list of specific requirements with the expectation that you’ll exactly replace someone on the team or fit a role defined by committee. MixRank is more pragmatic: we first get excited about bringing a unique individual onto the team, then figure out the best way to support their specific talents. Junior Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re looking for remote junior engineers with 0–3 years of professional software experience and 5+ years of curiosity exploring computers, programming, and technical hobby projects. This is an open-ended entry role with mentorship and diverse opportunities to work across all areas of our product: databases, distributed systems, infrastructure and tooling, data analysis, machine learning, frontend/backend web development, APIs, data mining, data modeling, and more. To stand out, please highlight what makes you unique: passion for computing, curiosity and side projects, work ethic, niche research, or anything else that shows how you think and build. Ideally, you’ve already graduated. But if you still have one or more years left of school, please feel free to apply anyway. If you’re the right fit for the team, we’ll figure out a way to accommodate your schedule. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/Fnwsojk-j Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re hiring generalist software engineers to work on web applications, data mining, machine learning/data science, data transformation/ETL, data modeling, database scaling, infrastructure, DevOps, and more. We’ll tailor the role to the subset of areas that best match your interests. Beneficial experience includes PostgreSQL, Python, Rust, Linux, TypeScript, Nix, frontend/backend web development, and data mining. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/RXQspen-s I’m Kiran, Chief of Staff at MixRank, a fully remote data startup building go-to-market intelligence. We’re US-incorporated but hire globally, and we’re bringing on new teammates to join a fast-moving team with real ownership and impact.

jobs.author: possibilistic
jobs.title: ArtCraft | Senior Engineers | SF (Onsite) / Atlanta (Onsite) | $150-$250k + Equity | https://getartcraft.com
jobs.text: Those fucking rent-seeking hyperscalers took the internet away from you, and we’re going to give it back to you and to everyone. Web 1.0 was great - we had IRC, file sharing, third party chat clients. There were personal websites, forums. Flash was a format kids could use. Everything supported embedding and uploading. Websites actually had APIs and RSS. File sharing, FTP, MP3s, discs, owned media. Broadband brought our parents and grandparents online, but the shift to the non-technical majority created an opportunity to grossly oversimplify everything. Everything dumbed down into a pre-packaged product. Startups began turning their offerings into walled gardens. Platforms took precedence over protocols. APIs and access and data export went away. And then the rent-seeking began. The era of ownership ended. Corporate Memphis. Jesus Christ. We’ve rallied a massive community to build MIT/Apache-licensed alternatives to Adobe, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Autodesk, SolidWorks, Slack, Discord, Unreal Engine, OpenRouter, RunPod, and more. The goal is full feature parity, with code anyone can own, inspect, modify, and build on. We’re digesting second-class apps and platforms into first-class applications, libraries, and APIs with full MCP support. We’re distilling out the good parts, and we’re building the connective tissue that draws them together. 100% of the internet is going to be open source soon, and we’re going to force it open. Loudly. We have eight figures in run rate revenue, over 20M app downloads and growing. Our community is the best part, and it’s energetic like a wildfire. Everyone resonates with our mission. We’re missionaries, not mercenaries. We are going to slay the incumbents by being better. Our motto is Google’s old motto - “Don't be evil (tm)”. We’re a tiny team looking for strong engineers to own major parts of the product: desktop apps, lots of completely open source backend infrastructure, agent workflows, agentic app factories. Stack: Rust, a sprinkle of TypeScript/React, egui, Tauri, MySQL/Postgres, Redis, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes. Lots and lots of Rust. We’re systems engineers by trade, but we like to vibe code Rust. Did I say Rust? Rust. Rust Rust Rust. Maybe that's a filter. You have to be self-directed and independent. If you want to open source Salesforce with half your time, do it! If you want to work on Solidworks 3D printing applications, great! Writing music apps and DAWs? Go for it! Custom Discord/Slack clients for our custom, completely open source chat API and platform? Hell yeah. Our organization is flat, and we're going to go after everybody and everything. Everything you build here will be open source. We have no private repos. We can reclaim the internet. That’s our mission. Want to know more about us? Look up “Adobe ArtCraft” on YouTube / TikTok / your platform of choice. If this resonates with you, email hn@storyteller.ai with your Github, a little about yourself and something you’ve built. Write the sentence, “don’t take my RAM, Sam!” so we know you’re one of the good guys.

stackOverflowQuestions.title: Safe pattern to process multiple files in Awk
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I'm re-writing a shell utility that takes three file arguments and cross-validate them with Awk. The Awk implementation is not guaranteed to be GNU so I need to stick to POSIX. The current code relies on FNR == 1 to set an input_no (equivalent to GNU ARGIND ) to keep track of the input that is processed, and some checks are run at the end of each input (equivalent to GNU ENDFILE ): #!/bin/bash sam_sq_to_tsv() { ...; } # output: SQ-SN \t SQ-LN fasta_to_tsv() { ...;} # output: id \t sequence awk -F '\t' ' FNR == 1 { if (input_no == 1) { if (!n_bam_recs) exit 1; } else if (input_no == 2) { if (!n_bed_recs) exit 1; } ++input_no; next; } input_no == 1 { ++n_bam_recs; # some SAM SQ header processing next; } input_no == 2 { if (!NF || /^#/) next; # skip comments/empty lines ++n_bed_recs; # some BED processing next; } input_no == 3 { ++n_fasta_recs; # some FASTA sequences processing next; } END { if (input_no != 3 || !n_fasta_recs) exit 1; # some cross-validations } ' \ "<(sam_sq_to_tsv -- "$1")" \ "$2" \ "<(fasta_to_tsv -- "$3")" But, the file arguments are provided by the user so a lot of issues can crop up; for eg.: if any of sam_sq_to_tsv -- "$1" / "$2" / fasta_to_tsv -- "$3" ends up empty then input_no won't be incremented at FNR == 1 and Awk will apply the wrong logic to the remaining inputs. if sam_sq_to_tsv / fasta_to_tsv fail during their processing then the error may be silently ignored by Awk. if $2 is of the form file2_DP=500.bed then it will be misinterpreted as a variable assignment instead of a filename. What I'm looking for is a robust way to detect/prevent all the above points, preferably with a fail-fast functionality (as the last input can contain hundreds of millions of records).

infoqArticles.description: Ankit Jain of Aviator told QCon San Francisco 2026 that line-by-line code review is already fading, since most review comments concern knowledge sharing rather than defects and over 75% of PRs merge without human review. infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

She discusses data prep with hard negatives, distributed InfoNCE loss training on H100 GPUs, automated hyperparameter tuning, and production evaluation using LLM-as-a-judge. By Rachel Shalom
infoqArticles.author: Rachel Shalom

infoqArticles.title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
infoqArticles.description: Microsoft released .NET 11 with a .NET MAUI update focused on product quality. CoreCLR is now the default runtime on all platforms, and XAML gets incremental hot reload, implicit namespaces and faster resource dictionaries. The release also adds device test templates and passkey support, and raises the minimum Android and Apple platform versions. By Edin Kapić
infoqArticles.author: Edin Kapić

infoqArticles.title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
infoqArticles.description: Mock Service Worker 3.0 is now ESM-only, requires Node.js 22 or later, and cuts package size from 416KB to 234KB. It adds GraphQL subscription support, protocol-specific entrypoints, and an experimental defineNetwork API. Node.js interception now works at the TCP and TLS level. Some users report test failures from newly intercepted OPTIONS preflight requests. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Recap of Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot as the Work OS and Agent Governance
infoqArticles.description: At Ignite 2026, Microsoft positioned Copilot as the operating system for work and extended agent identity, governance, and cost controls across Azure, Foundry, Entra, and Defender. infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR After Three-Year Migration
infoqArticles.description: GitHub migrated github.com from styled-components to CSS Modules over three years, reporting a 55% cut in server-side rendering time and 25% faster component initialisation. Primer components were converted behind feature flags, and about 7,760 sx prop usages were migrated with codemods and Copilot agents. Commenters questioned user impact and hashed class names. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
infoqArticles.description: DoorDash has redesigned its real-time dispatch platform, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. The new system delivers 10x higher throughput and more than 99.99% peak availability. It also supports hybrid machine learning inference and multi-agent reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize delivery assignments.

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Learning Out Loud (Under Near-Existential Pressure)

Leaders will discover actionable strategies to support their teams, debunk tech zealotry, and foster an adaptive engineering culture that thrives during upheaval.
infoqArticles.author: Laura Savino

infoqArticles.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts

infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis
